author: pep-m-java-methods-three-sme-final plus pep-m-java-methods-gift-sme-final-recheck (independent Java technology critics)

findings.claim: Feedback says a String return type would require returning a String on every path, but JLS SE 25 8.4.7 requires a return only on paths that can complete normally.
findings.recommendation: Say a compatible value is required on every path that can complete normally, while abrupt or non-completing paths need no return.

findings.claim: The unqualified-call distractor says the class name may be omitted only inside Geometry, although a subclass or static import also allows it; line 36 says no object exists, although main has objects and only a Player receiver is missing.
findings.recommendation: Bound the scenario to an unrelated class with no inheritance or static import, and say no Player object is available for the unqualified access.

findings.claim: The growing-String length(s + "x") scenario credits only StackOverflowError, but a focused JDK run produced either StackOverflowError or OutOfMemoryError depending on supported VM resource settings, so the key is not unique.
findings.recommendation: Use a recursive primitive scenario with no growing per-call allocation, or qualify the assumptions; do not mark OutOfMemoryError categorically impossible.

findings.claim: Step Over feedback says it runs the whole call and pauses at the next line, but IntelliJ IDEA Step Over stops at enabled breakpoints inside called methods; Force Step Over ignores them.
findings.recommendation: Say Step Over normally reaches the next caller line, but an enabled breakpoint inside the called method can stop it first.

findings.claim: count(n + 1) from 1 reaches 0 by int wraparound (JLS SE 25 15.18.2), and JVMS SE 25 2.5.2 sets no universal stack limit below that depth, so the categorical claim that the stack runs out first (lines 35-39 and 44) is not source-guaranteed.
findings.recommendation: State the permitted-stack resource assumption in the stem, or use a non-progressing step that wraparound cannot rescue; keep the HTML unchanged.

findings.claim: Resume feedback says Resume does not stop in the caller, but the next enabled breakpoint may be in the caller.
findings.recommendation: Say Resume has no caller-specific stopping behavior and runs to the next enabled breakpoint, which may be in the caller, or to program completion.
